W.note: Strict 5-7-5 (Lens cloud on the ridge = 5; the wind pours through it all day = 7; the cloud does not move = 5), and the lenticular cloud that stays put while wind runs through it is an accurate, well-chosen image with a real turn on stillness.

X.note: Strict 5-7-5 (Sil-ver threads at dusk = 5; clouds no com-mon sky can make = 7; hang where no one looks = 5), but the cloud type is never named or sharply seen, and 'silver threads' and 'sky can make' lean vague, though 'hang where no one looks' lands.

Y.note: Strict 5-7-5 (Na-cre-ous light blooms = 5; high a-bove the fro-zen fjord = 7; a cloud gone by dawn = 5), and naming nacreous (polar stratospheric) clouds over a frozen fjord at the right hour is precise and true to the phenomenon, with ephemerality as the closing turn.

Z.note: Counts 5-8-6 rather than 5-7-5 (Sun be-low the ridge = 5; the cloud's edge turns mo-ther-of-pearl = 8; then the blue takes it back = 6), so the shape is loose, but the sunset iridescence at the cloud edge is accurately evoked and 'the blue takes it back' gives a fine fading turn, with 'mother-of-pearl' a slightly stock phrase.
